The cold load reads and JSON-parses the fixture from disk inside the 100ms budget, so on a loaded/slow CI host `totalMs` can exceed 100ms and flake. The second assertion is also redundant with `totalMs` (it measures from the same starting point plus the intervening assertions) and equally host-dependent. Prefer asserting the deterministic contract (e.g. `installed`, `miss`, `cacheHit`, or a stubbed clock / injected budget) instead of raw wall-clock durations, or raise/relax the bound so it guards against real regressions rather than scheduling jitter.

packages/venue/src/index.ts.content:
The `LEFT`/`RIGHT`/`CENTER` thirding is not a valid partition and produces incorrect/overlapping target sets for small fixture counts:

The ranges are `LEFT = [0, ceil(n/3))`, `RIGHT = [n - ceil(n/3), n)`, `CENTER = [ceil(n/3), n - ceil(n/3))`.

- n = 1: `LEFT = [0]` and `RIGHT = [0]` — the same cell is returned by two different targets, so an operation applied to both (or a `LEFT` + `RIGHT` mapping) is applied twice.
- n = 2: `CENTER = [1, 1)` is empty.
- n = 4: `CENTER = [2, 2)` is empty while `LEFT`/`RIGHT` each take 2 cells.

`CENTER` silently becomes empty and `LEFT`/`RIGHT` can overlap, so callers get wrong target sets with no error. Please guard the boundaries (e.g. compute `third = Math.floor(n/3)` and clamp/deriving `CENTER` from the leftover after `LEFT`/`RIGHT`, or handle `n < 3` explicitly) so the three sets are disjoint and cover the intended cells.

`placeFixtures` re-looks-up every cell by scanning `fixtures` (O(f)) and then scanning `f.cells` (O(c)) for each of the N ordered cells, making this O(N * (f + c)) with two `find(...)!` non-null assertions. The assertions hide any mismatch (a ref produced by `globalCellOrder` that is not found would throw an unhandled `TypeError` rather than a graceful failure) and the whole method recomputes data `globalCellOrder` already visited. Prefer building a single `Map` keyed by `fixtureId`/`cellIndex` (or have `globalCellOrder` return the positions) to keep it O(N) and avoid the non-null assertions.

packages/venue/src/index.ts.content: The reserved target names `"ALL"`, `"LEFT"`, `"RIGHT"`, `"CENTER"` are duplicated here as magic string literals and again in the comparisons inside `resolveTarget`. Because `resolveTarget` checks these literals before falling back to group membership, any group actually named `ALL`/`LEFT`/`RIGHT`/`CENTER` in a fixture can never be targeted, and renaming/extending `DEFAULT_GROUPS` will not be reflected in the resolution logic. packages/venue/src/venue.test.ts.content: This case supplies a foreign file with BOTH an invalid format (`"other"`) AND an invalid version (`9`), so it cannot tell which guard actually fired. `importVenue` evaluates `file.format !== "autolight-venue" || file.version !== 1`; if the `format` check were deleted, the version guard (`9 !== 1`) would still throw the exact same message and the test stays green. The test therefore does not protect the format rejection path it claims to cover, and the `version: 9` value is useless for isolating the version path too. Split into independent cases (valid version + wrong format, and valid format + wrong version). Note also the title promises a "typed error" but only a message regex is asserted.

The round-trip is only asserted with `toEqual` on the whole object. `toEqual` deep-compares values, so it still passes when no serialization actually happens: if `exportVenue` stopped calling `structuredClone` and returned the same object/reference graph, `importVenue` would clone it and `toEqual` would remain green. This is precisely the regression the task's "delete test" targets, yet this test cannot detect it. Assert reference independence and exercise a real (string) round-trip so a missing/incorrect serializer fails the test.

Only a positive, already-in-range value (0.3) is checked, and the same `importVenue(exportVenue(venue))` expression is evaluated twice. `setLogicalZero` applies a modulo wrap (`((s % 1) + 1) % 1`), so a boundary/normalization case (e.g. 0 or -0.3 -> 0.7) is what would catch a broken wrap. Reuse a single result variable instead of recomputing the round-trip.

Two defects in this error path:
1) `pytest.skip()` raises `Skipped`, so the trailing `continue` is unreachable dead code.
2) Catching `subprocess.CalledProcessError` and converting it to a skip means a genuine transcode/encode failure (e.g. a bad flag or broken ffmpeg build) silently turns the whole test into a pass-by-skip, and because the skip aborts the loop it also drops coverage for every remaining codec. Only skip when the codec is truly unavailable (e.g. probe the encoder first); otherwise let the exception fail the test.

This only checks that the four durations agree with each other; it never verifies the expected absolute duration (~1.0 s). A pipeline that consistently returns a wrong duration for every codec (truncated, doubled, or mis-scaled output) would still pass. Also, for lossy codecs (MP3/AAC) encoder priming/padding can shift the duration near the 0.05 s threshold, making the relative comparison flaky. Assert the absolute duration against the known signal length as well, with a tolerance that accounts for codec delay.
